title: RAW_UNREVIEWED: fixed-star rise and set distinguish daily concealment from first-or-last visibility with a solar interval
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_UNSELECTED_NOT_TESTED. Complete Pliny XVIII.218–219 explicitly distinguishes two senses of stellar rising/setting: daily concealment by the arriving Sun and emergence after its departure, versus the day a fixed star first begins or ceases to appear near sunrise or sunset. The second account assigns morning/evening names and requires a stated minimum three-quarter-hour interval before sunrise or after sunset for seeing the stars. A whole-unit working interpretation must retain both event types, the observer-visible state, the minimum interval and the fixed-star scope. No named star, Voynich group, target passage, modern visibility threshold or confirmed semantic binding is claimed. This is related to IDEA000678 first/last appearance and IDEA000743 persistent hidden body, but adds a source-explicit distinction between two event constructors plus an observation threshold; novelty remains unreviewed. Electronic ancient Latin layer, no medieval image/transmission claim.

design.mechanism: The same fixed-star discussion separates daily Sun-caused concealment/emergence from first-or-last appearance on a day near dawn/dusk; the latter visible event requires a lower-bounded interval relative to the solar event.
design.unit: Complete Pliny Naturalis historia XVIII.218–219; any future target application must cover a whole prospectively chosen already-admitted unit, none selected here.
design.contrast: A two-event account with an observer-visible state and minimum solar interval versus one generic physical rise/set or unconditional daily visibility cycle that collapses first/last dates, interval and fixed-star scope.
design.prediction: A future frozen whole-unit reading must distinguish the ordinary daily masking pair from first/last-visible-day events, retain morning/evening relative timing and the stated minimum three-quarter-hour interval, and not silently substitute moving Venus/Mercury for the fixed-star subject.
design.scope: Source-only raw content hypothesis; target unbound, no selected experiment or new admission.

source_evidence.quote:
**§218.** Omnis autem ratio observata est tribus modis, exortu siderum occasuque et ipsorum temporum cardinibus. exortus occasusque binis modis intelleguntur. aut enim adventu solis occultantur stellae et conspici desinunt aut eiusdem abscessu proferunt se, ut emersum hoc melius quam exortum consuetudo dixisset et illud occultationem potius quam occasum.

**§219.** alio modo, quo die incipiunt apparere vel desinunt oriente sole aut occidente, matutini vespertinive cognominati, prout alteruter eorum mane vel crepusculo contingit. dodrantes horarum, cum minimum, intervalla ea desiderant ante solis ortum vel post occasum, ut aspici possint. praeterea bis quaedam exoriuntur et occidunt, omnisque sermo de iis est stellis, quas adhaerere caelo diximus.
